newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Calendar spreads bought in BP, Shell.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Calendar spreads bought in BP, Shell.

text.p: The main stock options trades by late afternoon on Monday were bearish calendar spreads in oil giants British Petroleum and Shell Transport & Trading, dealers said.
The deals took advantage of a share price rise and near-term puts were sold in order to buy longer-term puts betting that the underlying shares will decline over the long-term.
In BP, a spread was established by selling 550 October 600 puts at 4p and buying 550 April 600 puts at 19p.
Similarly the spread in Shell consisted of selling 500 October 950 puts at 30p and buying 500 April 950 puts at 52p.
By 1330 GMT, BP shares added 6p to 628-1/2p while those of Shell were up 8-1/2p to 941p.

The chief deal in confectionery and beverages group Cadbury Schweppes was a three-for-five ratioed diagonal spread which involved buying 300 November 420 calls at 94p and selling 500 May 500 calls at 43p.
The net debit was 67p per strategy and in general if Cadbury shares rise by November expiry the spread will increase to make a profit.
Over in Barclays Bank one trader bought stock and hedged it by a split synthetic short sale through stock options.
The synthetic short comprised of selling 250 December 950 calls at 26-1/2p and buying 250 December 850 puts at 10-1/2p.

At the December expiry if the shares fall below 850p, losses from the cash position will be offset by gains from the puts and if the shares go above 950p the gains from the stock will be offset by losses from the short calls.
Barclays' shares fell 3p to 907-1/2p and those of Cadbury Schweppes were a penny better at 513-1/2p.
